title: Architecture, Design & Trade-offs
sub: System design, patterns, scalability and the trade-offs behind them.

cards.def:
The overall structure and design of a system
हिंदी: प्रणाली की समग्र संरचना
examples: The architecture separates ingestion from transformation.
Draw the architecture on one page before the design review.
The new architecture lets each team deploy on its own.
A simple architecture is easier to debug at 2 am.

cards.def:
The arrangement of components and their connections
हिंदी: घटकों की संरचनात्मक व्यवस्था
examples: The network topology limits how we can scale.
The office network topology has one main switch per floor.
Changing the cluster topology needs a maintenance window.
Ask the platform team for a diagram of the current topology.

cards.def:
A single, tightly integrated application
हिंदी: एकल विशाल एप्लिकेशन
examples: We are slowly breaking the monolith into services.
For a small startup, a monolith is often the right choice.
Every change to the monolith needs a full regression test.
The monolith takes forty minutes to build and deploy.

cards.def:
A small independently deployable service
हिंदी: छोटी स्वतंत्र सेवा
examples: Each microservice owns its own data store.
The payment microservice can be released without touching the rest.
Too many microservices can make debugging harder.
Each microservice has its own team and on-call rota.

cards.def:
An infrastructure layer managing service-to-service communication
हिंदी: सेवाओं के बीच संचार प्रबंधन परत
examples: The service mesh handles retries and encryption.
The service mesh gives us traffic metrics between services.
We added a service mesh to encrypt all internal traffic.
Debugging the service mesh config took the whole afternoon.

cards.def:
Based on producing and reacting to events
हिंदी: घटना-आधारित
examples: We moved to an event-driven design to decouple vendors.
In an event-driven system, services react to order events.
Event-driven designs are hard to trace without good logging.
The notification service is fully event-driven.

cards.def:
A pattern where publishers send messages to subscribers via a broker
हिंदी: प्रकाशक-ग्राहक संदेश पैटर्न
examples: Pub-sub lets many consumers react to the same event.
We use pub-sub so billing and emails both get the order event.
With pub-sub, the sender doesn't know who is listening.
Adding a new subscriber in pub-sub doesn't change the publisher.

cards.def:
Middleware that routes messages between systems
हिंदी: संदेशों को आगे पहुँचाने वाला मध्यस्थ
examples: Kafka acts as our message broker.
The message broker stores events until consumers read them.
If the message broker goes down, orders stop flowing.
RabbitMQ is a popular message broker for smaller systems.

cards.def:
How far a consumer is behind the latest message
हिंदी: उपभोक्ता का पीछे रह जाना
examples: Rising consumer lag means we're falling behind.
Consumer lag jumped during the sale, so we added more consumers.
Set an alert when consumer lag crosses ten thousand messages.
Consumer lag returned to zero after the backlog cleared.

cards.def:
A subset of data split for parallel processing
हिंदी: डेटा का हिस्सा
examples: Messages with the same key go to the same partition.
Add more partitions so more consumers can read in parallel.
One hot partition slowed down the whole topic.
The table is split into one partition per month.

cards.def:
Splitting a database into smaller independent parts
हिंदी: डेटाबेस को टुकड़ों में बाँटना
examples: Sharding by vendor ID spreads the load evenly.
Sharding helped us handle millions of users in one database.
Sharding makes cross-customer reports more complex.
We chose sharding by region to keep data local.

cards.def:
Copying data across multiple nodes
हिंदी: डेटा की प्रतिलिपि बनाना
examples: Replication provides durability if a node fails.
Replication across two data centres protects us from a regional outage.
Replication lag means the read copy may be a few seconds old.
Check replication status before switching to the standby.

cards.def:
Guarantee that all readers see the same data
हिंदी: डेटा की एकरूपता
examples: Strong consistency costs us some latency.
Bank balances need strong consistency, not approximate numbers.
We traded some consistency for faster page loads.
Consistency issues showed different prices on web and app.

cards.def:
A model where data becomes consistent over time
हिंदी: समय के साथ एकरूप होने वाला मॉडल
examples: Reports tolerate eventual consistency of a few seconds.
The like count uses eventual consistency, so it may lag a little.
With eventual consistency, all replicas match within seconds.
Explain eventual consistency to the business team before launch.

cards.def:
The guarantee that committed data persists
हिंदी: डेटा के बचे रहने की गारंटी
examples: The queue offers durability even if the broker restarts.
Durability means a confirmed order is never lost.
We write to disk before replying to guarantee durability.
Backups add another layer of durability.

cards.def:
The proportion of time a system is operational and accessible
हिंदी: उपलब्धता
examples: The design favours availability over strict consistency.
Our target availability is 99.9 percent per month.
Running in two regions improves availability.
The SLA defines availability for business hours only.

cards.def:
The ability to function despite network splits
हिंदी: नेटवर्क विभाजन में भी चलने की क्षमता
examples: Any distributed system must handle partition tolerance.
Partition tolerance matters when two data centres lose connection.
Without partition tolerance, a network split would stop the system.
We tested partition tolerance by cutting the link between regions.

cards.def:
Principle that you cannot have all of consistency, availability and partition tolerance
हिंदी: कैप सिद्धांत
examples: The CAP theorem forces trade-offs in distributed design.
The CAP theorem came up in my system design interview.
Because of the CAP theorem, we chose availability for the catalogue.
The CAP theorem helps explain why perfect systems don't exist.

cards.def:
Adding more machines to handle load
हिंदी: मशीनें बढ़ाकर क्षमता बढ़ाना
examples: Horizontal scaling suits our stateless workers.
Horizontal scaling let us add servers during the festival sale.
Horizontal scaling is easier when the app is stateless.
Cloud platforms make horizontal scaling almost automatic.

cards.def:
Adding more power to an existing machine
हिंदी: मशीन की शक्ति बढ़ाना
examples: Vertical scaling hits a ceiling quickly.
Vertical scaling was the quickest fix: we doubled the memory.
Vertical scaling gets expensive with very large machines.
We used vertical scaling until the database hit its limit.

cards.def:
Not retaining information between requests
हिंदी: पिछली स्थिति न रखने वाला
examples: Keep the workers stateless so they can scale freely.
A stateless API is easy to run behind a load balancer.
Store sessions in Redis so the web servers stay stateless.
Stateless services can restart without losing anything.

cards.def:
Retaining information between requests
हिंदी: स्थिति को सहेजने वाला
examples: Stateful services are harder to scale and recover.
The database is stateful, so we back it up carefully.
Stateful workloads need persistent storage in Kubernetes.
A stateful service needs a plan for moving its data.

cards.def:
A component that distributes traffic across servers
हिंदी: ट्रैफ़िक बाँटने वाला घटक
examples: The load balancer removes unhealthy nodes automatically.
The load balancer sends traffic to three web servers.
Health checks tell the load balancer which servers are alive.
A misconfigured load balancer sent all traffic to one node.

cards.def:
Temporary storage for fast data retrieval
हिंदी: तेज़ पहुँच हेतु अस्थायी भंडारण
examples: A cache cut read latency by eighty percent.
The browser cache made the second page load instant.
Clear the cache if you still see the old design.
We cache product details for five minutes.

cards.def:
To mark cached data as no longer valid
हिंदी: कैश डेटा को अमान्य करना
examples: We invalidate the cache whenever a price is corrected.
Invalidate the CDN cache after updating the homepage images.
We forgot to invalidate the cache, so users saw old prices.
The service invalidates a user's cache when they change settings.

cards.def:
Removal of items from a cache to free space
हिंदी: कैश से डेटा हटाना
examples: Poor eviction policy caused frequent misses.
The cache uses least-recently-used eviction.
Too much eviction means the cache is too small.
Monitor eviction rates during peak traffic.

cards.def:
The duration after which data expires
हिंदी: डेटा की वैधता अवधि
examples: Set the time-to-live to one hour.
A short time-to-live keeps the data fresh but increases load.
The DNS record has a time-to-live of five minutes.
Login tokens have a time-to-live of one day.

cards.def:
An ordered list of tasks awaiting processing
हिंदी: कतार
examples: Failed messages go to a dead-letter queue.
Email sending runs through a queue so the page stays fast.
The queue grew to a million jobs during the outage.
Workers pick tasks from the queue one at a time.

cards.def:
A queue for messages that couldn't be processed
हिंदी: असफल संदेशों की कतार
examples: We review the dead-letter queue every morning.
Messages with bad data end up in the dead-letter queue.
Set an alert if the dead-letter queue starts growing.
We replayed the dead-letter queue after fixing the bug.

cards.def:
A mechanism to slow producers when consumers are overwhelmed
हिंदी: दबाव नियंत्रण तंत्र
examples: Backpressure prevents the queue from overflowing.
Without backpressure, the fast producer crashed the slow consumer.
The library handles backpressure automatically.
Backpressure kept memory usage stable under heavy load.

cards.def:
Processing data in groups at scheduled intervals
हिंदी: समूहों में डेटा प्रसंस्करण
examples: Batch processing suits the nightly vendor files.
Salary calculations run as batch processing at month end.
Batch processing is cheaper than processing each record instantly.
The batch processing job finished an hour late last night.

cards.def:
Processing data continuously as it arrives
हिंदी: निरंतर डेटा प्रसंस्करण
examples: Stream processing gives us near real-time updates.
Fraud detection needs stream processing, not nightly batches.
Stream processing updates the dashboard every second.
We use Flink for stream processing of click events.

cards.def:
A series of connected processing stages
हिंदी: चरणबद्ध प्रसंस्करण शृंखला
examples: Each stage of the pipeline can be tested separately.
The CI pipeline runs tests on every pull request.
Our data pipeline loads sales data every hour.
A broken step stopped the whole pipeline.

cards.def:
A unique token ensuring a request is processed once
हिंदी: एक बार प्रसंस्करण सुनिश्चित करने वाली कुंजी
examples: Attach an idempotency key to every payment request.
The mobile app sends an idempotency key with every order.
Without an idempotency key, a retry could charge the card twice.
Store each idempotency key for at least a day.

cards.def:
Guaranteeing each message is processed one time only
हिंदी: ठीक एक बार प्रसंस्कृत
examples: Exactly-once delivery is hard to guarantee end to end.
Exactly-once processing matters for payment events.
The vendor claims exactly-once delivery, but we still check for duplicates.
Exactly-once semantics add latency and complexity.

cards.def:
Guaranteeing delivery but allowing duplicates
हिंदी: कम से कम एक बार
examples: At-least-once delivery requires idempotent consumers.
The queue offers at-least-once delivery, so duplicates can happen.
With at-least-once delivery, design consumers to ignore repeats.
At-least-once is the default for most message brokers.

cards.def:
Treated as a single all-or-nothing operation
हिंदी: लेन-देन आधारित
examples: The update must be transactional to avoid partial writes.
Money transfers must be transactional: debit and credit together.
The transactional update rolled back when the second step failed.
Use a transactional outbox to publish events safely.

cards.def:
Indivisible; either fully completes or not at all
हिंदी: अविभाज्य
examples: The write is atomic, so no half-saved records appear.
Renaming a file is atomic on most file systems.
Make the counter update atomic to avoid lost increments.
The deployment switch is atomic, so users never see half a release.

cards.def:
Separation of concurrent operations to avoid interference
हिंदी: समवर्ती कार्यों का पृथक्करण
examples: Higher isolation reduces anomalies but costs performance.
Transaction isolation stops one user from seeing another's half-done update.
We lowered the isolation level to improve throughput.
Test isolation means one test can't affect another.

cards.def:
Organising data to reduce redundancy
हिंदी: डेटा की अनावश्यक पुनरावृत्ति घटाना
examples: Normalisation keeps the reference data consistent.
Normalisation split customer and address data into separate tables.
Too much normalisation can make simple reports slow.
The normalisation step removed duplicate city names.

cards.def:
To add redundancy to data to improve read speed
हिंदी: पढ़ने की गति हेतु डेटा दोहराना
examples: We denormalised the table to avoid expensive joins.
We denormalise order data into the reporting database.
Denormalise carefully, because updates must change several places.
The search index denormalises product and price details.

cards.def:
A structure that speeds up data lookup
हिंदी: खोज तेज़ करने वाली संरचना
examples: Adding an index cut the query from minutes to seconds.
Add an index on the email column for faster login lookups.
Too many indexes slow down inserts.
The book's index helped me find the topic quickly.

cards.def:
The database's strategy for executing a query
हिंदी: क्वेरी निष्पादन योजना
examples: The query plan shows a full table scan.
Check the query plan before adding more hardware.
The query plan changed after the statistics were updated.
A good query plan uses the index instead of scanning everything.

cards.def:
Changing a data structure over time without breaking consumers
हिंदी: डेटा संरचना में क्रमिक बदलाव
examples: Schema evolution rules prevent breaking changes.
Plan for schema evolution from day one.
Avro supports schema evolution with default values.
Schema evolution let us add fields without breaking old apps.

cards.def:
The record of where data came from and how it changed
हिंदी: डेटा की उत्पत्ति और बदलाव का रिकॉर्ड
examples: Data lineage helps auditors trace each number.
Data lineage shows which source fed this dashboard number.
Without data lineage, fixing a wrong report takes days.
The new tool draws data lineage automatically.

cards.def:
The accuracy, completeness and reliability of data
हिंदी: डेटा की गुणवत्ता
examples: Poor data quality undermines trust in reports.
We run data quality checks before loading the warehouse.
Data quality issues came from manual entry at branches.
The data quality score is shown on every report.

cards.def:
The authoritative origin of a piece of data
हिंदी: प्रामाणिक डेटा स्रोत
examples: The instrument master is the source of truth.
The HR system is the source of truth for employee details.
Two sources of truth always lead to arguments.
Update the source of truth, not the copies.

cards.def:
The single, most accurate version of an entity's data
हिंदी: सबसे सटीक एकल रिकॉर्ड
examples: We merge vendor data into a golden record.
The golden record combines details from sales and support.
Building a golden record for each customer took months.
Reports should always use the golden record.

cards.def:
Core business data shared across systems
हिंदी: मुख्य साझा व्यावसायिक डेटा
examples: Master data management removes conflicting copies.
Customer and product lists are part of master data.
Errors in master data spread to every downstream system.
A small team owns master data changes.

cards.def:
Adding extra information to existing data
हिंदी: डेटा में अतिरिक्त जानकारी जोड़ना
examples: Enrichment adds sector and currency to each record.
Address enrichment adds the pin code and district.
Enrichment with weather data improved our demand forecast.
The enrichment step runs after validation.

cards.def:
To convert data to a common standard format
हिंदी: डेटा को मानक रूप में बदलना
examples: We normalise vendor formats into one canonical model.
Normalise phone numbers so they all start with the country code.
The script normalises dates into one format.
We normalise customer names before matching duplicates.

cards.def:
Standard and authoritative
हिंदी: मानक / प्रामाणिक
examples: All vendors map to one canonical schema.
The canonical order format is shared by all teams.
Map every vendor field to its canonical name.
Store a canonical copy and convert only when exporting.

cards.def:
To convert data into a format for storage or transmission
हिंदी: डेटा को संग्रहण योग्य रूप देना
examples: Avro is used to serialise the messages.
We serialise the user object to JSON before saving it.
Serialising large objects can be slow.
The cache stores serialised responses for quick reuse.

cards.def:
To convert stored data back into objects
हिंदी: संग्रहीत डेटा को वापस वस्तु रूप देना
examples: Deserialisation failed due to a missing field.
The app deserialises the JSON response into a user object.
We deserialise messages using the schema registry.
An old client couldn't deserialise the new field type.

cards.def:
An entry point that manages access to services
हिंदी: प्रवेश द्वार
examples: All external calls pass through the API gateway.
The payment gateway connects our shop to the bank.
The gateway checks the token before passing requests on.
We added rate limits at the gateway level.

cards.def:
A URL where a service can be accessed
हिंदी: सेवा का पता
examples: The endpoint returns data in JSON format.
The login endpoint returns a token if the password is correct.
Document every endpoint with examples.
The health endpoint tells us if the service is alive.

cards.def:
The amount of data in a request or message
हिंदी: संदेश में डेटा की मात्रा
examples: Large payload sizes slow down the queue.
Compress images to reduce payload size on mobile networks.
The API rejects requests above a certain payload size.
We reduced payload size by sending only the changed fields.

cards.def:
A cap on the number of requests allowed in a period
हिंदी: अनुरोधों की अधिकतम सीमा
examples: The vendor's rate limit blocks bulk downloads.
We hit the rate limit and had to wait a minute.
Each customer has a rate limit of one thousand calls per hour.
Add a rate limit to the login page to stop attacks.

cards.def:
A pattern that stops calls to a failing service
हिंदी: विफल सेवा को कॉल रोकने वाला पैटर्न
examples: The circuit breaker opened after five consecutive failures.
The circuit breaker stops us from flooding a broken service.
After thirty seconds, the circuit breaker tries again.
Add a circuit breaker around the slow vendor API.

cards.def:
Isolation of components so one failure doesn't spread
हिंदी: विफलता को फैलने से रोकने वाला पृथक्करण
examples: A bulkhead keeps one vendor's issue from affecting others.
Separate thread pools act as a bulkhead between services.
A bulkhead design limits the damage from one slow dependency.
We added a bulkhead so reports can't starve live traffic.

cards.def:
To attempt an operation again after failure
हिंदी: दोबारा प्रयास करना
examples: The job retries three times before alerting.
The app will retry the upload when the network returns.
Don't retry forever; set a maximum number of attempts.
Each retry waits a little longer than the last.

cards.def:
A limit on how long to wait before giving up
हिंदी: प्रतीक्षा की अधिकतम अवधि
examples: The timeout was too short for large files.
The page shows a timeout error after thirty seconds.
Set a timeout on every external call.
We increased the timeout for the monthly report.

cards.def:
A periodic signal showing a service is alive
हिंदी: सेवा जीवित होने का संकेत
examples: Missing heartbeats triggered the failover.
Each worker sends a heartbeat every ten seconds.
No heartbeat for a minute means the node is marked dead.
The heartbeat dashboard shows which agents are online.

cards.def:
A test to see if a service is functioning
हिंदी: सेवा की स्थिति की जाँच
examples: The health check failed after the memory spike.
The load balancer runs a health check every five seconds.
Make the health check test the database connection too.
A failing health check removed the server from rotation.

cards.def:
Stopping a service after finishing in-progress work
हिंदी: चल रहे काम पूरे कर बंद करना
examples: Graceful shutdown prevents half-processed files.
Graceful shutdown lets current users finish their payments.
Kubernetes waits thirty seconds for graceful shutdown.
Without graceful shutdown, deploys caused failed requests.

cards.def:
Delay when a function or service starts from idle
हिंदी: निष्क्रिय से शुरू होने में देरी
examples: Lambda cold starts affected our response time.
The first request after a quiet night suffers a cold start.
We keep one instance warm to avoid cold starts.
Java functions usually have a longer cold start.

cards.def:
Running code without managing servers
हिंदी: सर्वरलेस
examples: Serverless suits spiky, unpredictable workloads.
With serverless, we pay only when code actually runs.
Our image resizing runs as a serverless function.
Serverless isn't ideal for long-running jobs.

cards.def:
To package an application with its dependencies
हिंदी: कंटेनर में पैक करना
examples: We containerised the parser for consistent deployment.
Containerise the app so it runs the same on every laptop.
We containerised the old service before moving it to the cloud.
Containerising tests made the CI builds more reliable.

cards.def:
Automated coordination of services and tasks
हिंदी: सेवाओं का स्वचालित समन्वय
examples: Kubernetes handles container orchestration.
Workflow orchestration tools schedule our nightly data jobs.
Orchestration restarts failed containers automatically.
Good orchestration hides a lot of operational work.

cards.def:
Managing infrastructure through versioned configuration files
हिंदी: कोड से इन्फ्रास्ट्रक्चर प्रबंधन
examples: Infrastructure as code makes environments reproducible.
With infrastructure as code, every change goes through code review.
We rebuilt the test environment in minutes using infrastructure as code.
Infrastructure as code removes manual clicking in the console.

cards.def:
Unchangeable after creation
हिंदी: अपरिवर्तनीय
examples: We deploy immutable images rather than patching servers.
Immutable servers are replaced, never edited by hand.
Make the config object immutable so nobody changes it by mistake.
Immutable backups protect us from ransomware.

cards.def:
Existing only for a short time
हिंदी: अल्पकालिक
examples: Ephemeral environments are created for each pull request.
Ephemeral storage is lost when the container restarts.
Use ephemeral test databases that delete themselves after the run.
Ephemeral credentials expire after one hour.

cards.def:
Serving multiple customers from one shared system
हिंदी: एक ही सिस्टम से कई ग्राहकों को सेवा देने वाला
examples: A multi-tenant design lowers cost per client.
Most SaaS products are multi-tenant.
In a multi-tenant system, one noisy client can affect others.
We moved from single-tenant to multi-tenant to save costs.

cards.def:
Keeping each customer's data separate
हिंदी: ग्राहकों के डेटा का पृथक्करण
examples: Tenant isolation is a strict security requirement.
Every query filters by customer ID to ensure tenant isolation.
Big banks often pay extra for stronger tenant isolation.
A bug in tenant isolation could leak one client's data to another.

cards.def:
Granting only the minimum access required
हिंदी: न्यूनतम आवश्यक अधिकार
examples: Apply least privilege to all service accounts.
Under least privilege, interns get read-only access.
Review permissions every quarter to keep least privilege.
Least privilege limits the damage if a password is stolen.

cards.def:
Protecting stored data by encrypting it
हिंदी: संग्रहीत डेटा का एन्क्रिप्शन
examples: Encryption at rest is mandatory for client data.
The cloud provider offers encryption at rest by default.
Auditors asked for proof of encryption at rest.
Laptops must use encryption at rest in case they're stolen.

cards.def:
Verifying who a user or system is
हिंदी: पहचान सत्यापन
examples: Authentication is handled by the central identity provider.
The app uses fingerprint authentication.
Two-factor authentication adds an extra layer of safety.
Authentication failed because the token had expired.

cards.def:
Determining what an authenticated user may do
हिंदी: अनुमतियों का निर्धारण
examples: Authorisation checks happen at every endpoint.
Authorisation rules decide who can approve payments.
The user logged in but failed the authorisation check.
Keep authorisation logic in one place, not spread everywhere.

cards.def:
A right to access a particular resource or data
हिंदी: डेटा/संसाधन तक पहुँच का अधिकार
examples: Vendor entitlements restrict who can view the data.
Check the user's entitlement before showing premium reports.
Entitlements are updated when a subscription changes.
She asked IT for an entitlement to the finance folder.

cards.def:
A weakness that could be exploited
हिंदी: कमज़ोरी
examples: The scan found a critical vulnerability in the library.
Update your phone to fix the latest security vulnerability.
Report any vulnerability to the security team privately.
The vulnerability was patched within a day.

cards.def:
The total points where a system could be attacked
हिंदी: हमले के संभावित बिंदु
examples: Removing unused endpoints shrinks the attack surface.
Every new integration adds to our attack surface.
Closing unused ports reduces the attack surface.

हिंदी: सबसे अधिक चलने वाला कोड भाग
examples: Avoid allocations on the hot path.
Logging inside the hot path slowed every request.
Optimise the hot path first; it runs millions of times a day.
Keep database calls out of the hot path where possible.

cards.def:
A part of a system under heavy use or load
हिंदी: सबसे अधिक भार वाला हिस्सा
examples: One partition became a hot spot.
The popular product page became a hot spot during the sale.
A hot spot on one server caused uneven load.
Spread keys evenly to avoid a hot spot.

cards.def:
Uneven distribution of data across partitions
हिंदी: डेटा का असमान वितरण
examples: Data skew caused one worker to lag.
Data skew meant one region had most of the records.
Salting the keys helped reduce data skew.
The job was slow because of data skew in one partition.

cards.def:
The number of distinct values in a data set
हिंदी: अलग-अलग मानों की संख्या
examples: High cardinality makes this index expensive.
Gender has low cardinality, but user ID has very high cardinality.
Avoid high cardinality labels in your metrics.
Check the cardinality before choosing an index.

cards.def:
Loading data only when it is needed
हिंदी: ज़रूरत पड़ने पर ही डेटा लोड करना
examples: Lazy loading improved start-up time.
Lazy loading images makes long pages load faster.
Lazy loading caused extra queries when we opened each order.
The app uses lazy loading for rarely used screens.

cards.def:
Loading related data in advance
हिंदी: संबंधित डेटा पहले से लोड करना
examples: Eager loading avoids repeated queries.
Eager loading fetched the orders with their items in one query.
Use eager loading when you know you'll need the related data.
Too much eager loading can slow the first page.

cards.def:
Failure to close connections after use
हिंदी: कनेक्शन बंद न करना
examples: A connection leak exhausted the database limit.
We found the connection leak in a missing close call.
A connection leak slowly used up all database connections.
Use try-with-resources to avoid a connection leak.

cards.def:
Rough and quick, as if calculated informally
हिंदी: मोटा और त्वरित अनुमान
examples: A back-of-the-envelope estimate shows ten terabytes a year.
A back-of-the-envelope calculation shows we need two servers.
Do a back-of-the-envelope estimate before ordering hardware.
Interviewers like back-of-the-envelope maths in design questions.

cards.def:
A process to choose one node to coordinate others
हिंदी: समन्वयक नोड चुनने की प्रक्रिया
examples: Leader election takes a few seconds after failure.
Leader election ensures only one node runs the scheduled job.
ZooKeeper is often used for leader election.
Leader election failed when the network was unstable.

cards.def:
A fault where two parts of a system act independently
हिंदी: दो हिस्सों का स्वतंत्र काम करना
examples: A network partition caused a split brain.
In a split brain, two nodes both think they are the leader.
Split brain can corrupt data if both sides accept writes.
We use a quorum to prevent split brain.

cards.def:
A method for nodes to agree on a value
हिंदी: नोड्स में सहमति का तरीका
examples: Raft is a widely used consensus protocol.
A consensus protocol keeps all replicas in agreement.
Paxos is a famous but complex consensus protocol.
Without a consensus protocol, nodes could disagree on the data.

cards.def:
A method where nodes spread information to peers
हिंदी: नोड्स द्वारा जानकारी फैलाने की विधि
examples: The cluster uses a gossip protocol for membership.
The gossip protocol spreads updates like office rumours.
With a gossip protocol, every node learns about failures quickly.
Cassandra uses a gossip protocol between nodes.

cards.def:
Strong dependence between components
हिंदी: घटकों की कसकर निर्भरता
examples: Tight coupling made the release risky.
Tight coupling between teams slowed every decision.
We removed tight coupling by adding a message queue.
Tight coupling to one vendor's API made switching hard.

cards.def:
Weak dependence allowing independent change
हिंदी: घटकों की ढीली निर्भरता
examples: Loose coupling lets teams deploy independently.
Loose coupling makes it easier to replace parts later.
Events help achieve loose coupling between services.
The design aims for loose coupling and high cohesion.

cards.def:
Making too many small network calls
हिंदी: ज़रूरत से ज़्यादा छोटे कॉल करने वाला
examples: The chatty API slowed the page load.
The chatty app made fifty calls just to load the home screen.
Combine requests to make the API less chatty.
A chatty design hurts users on slow mobile networks.

cards.def:
Sending one request to many downstream recipients
हिंदी: एक अनुरोध का कई जगह जाना
examples: Fan-out to ten services increased latency.
One tweet causes a fan-out to millions of followers.
Limit fan-out to keep the response time low.
The fan-out sends the order to billing, stock and email services.

cards.def:
Combining many inputs into one
हिंदी: कई इनपुट का एक में मिलना
examples: Fan-in aggregates results from all vendors.
The fan-in step merges results from three searches.
Fan-in waits until all workers finish.
Use a fan-in queue to collect results from many jobs.

cards.def:
A helper container deployed alongside the main service
हिंदी: मुख्य सेवा के साथ चलने वाला सहायक कंटेनर
examples: A sidecar handles logging and security.
The sidecar collects logs and sends them to our log server.
Istio adds a sidecar to every pod.
A sidecar lets us add features without changing the app.

cards.def:
A server that forwards client requests to backend servers
हिंदी: अनुरोध आगे भेजने वाला सर्वर
examples: The reverse proxy terminates TLS.
Nginx works as a reverse proxy in front of our app.
The reverse proxy also caches static files.
Configure the reverse proxy to pass the user's real IP.

cards.def:
A network of servers that delivers content from nearby locations
हिंदी: पास के सर्वर से सामग्री पहुँचाने वाला नेटवर्क
examples: A content delivery network cut page load time.
Videos load faster thanks to a content delivery network.
The content delivery network serves images from servers near users.
We put the website behind a content delivery network for the sale.

cards.def:
Low-cost storage for rarely accessed data
हिंदी: कम उपयोग वाले डेटा का सस्ता भंडारण
examples: Old files move to cold storage after ninety days.
Tax records move to cold storage after the audit year.
Cold storage is cheap, but restoring files takes hours.
We moved old videos to cold storage to cut costs.

cards.def:
Fast storage for frequently accessed data
हिंदी: बार-बार उपयोग वाले डेटा का तेज़ भंडारण
examples: Recent prices stay in hot storage.
Keep this month's orders in hot storage for fast reports.
Hot storage costs more but responds in milliseconds.
User profile photos are kept in hot storage.

cards.def:
Rules for how long data is kept
हिंदी: डेटा रखने की अवधि संबंधी नियम
examples: Our retention policy keeps raw files for seven years.
Our retention policy deletes chat logs after one year.
Check the retention policy before deleting old emails.
Different countries need different retention policies.

cards.def:
The requirement to store data in a particular region
हिंदी: डेटा का निर्धारित क्षेत्र में रहना
examples: Data residency rules limit where we host.
Data residency rules require Indian payment data to stay in India.
The client asked about data residency before signing.
Data residency affects which cloud region we choose.

cards.def:
Replacing sensitive data with non-sensitive tokens
हिंदी: संवेदनशील डेटा को टोकन से बदलना
examples: Tokenisation protects client account numbers.
Card tokenisation means shops never store your real card number.
Tokenisation reduces the impact of a data breach.
The payment app uses tokenisation for saved cards.

cards.def:
Hiding parts of sensitive data
हिंदी: संवेदनशील डेटा छुपाना
examples: Masking prevents leaks in test environments.
Masking shows only the last four digits of the card.
Apply masking to phone numbers in support screens.
Data masking lets developers test with realistic data safely.

cards.def:
Removing personal identifiers from data
हिंदी: व्यक्तिगत पहचान हटाना
examples: Anonymisation is required before sharing datasets.
Anonymisation lets researchers study health data safely.
Simple anonymisation isn't enough if records can be linked.
We did anonymisation before sharing survey results.

cards.def:
A security model that verifies every request
हिंदी: हर अनुरोध की पुष्टि करने वाला सुरक्षा मॉडल
examples: Zero trust assumes no network is safe.
Under zero trust, even office laptops must log in every time.
Zero trust became popular when remote work grew.
Our zero trust plan includes device checks.

cards.def:
The boundary of a protected network
हिंदी: सुरक्षित नेटवर्क की सीमा
examples: Security can't rely only on the perimeter.
The firewall protects the network perimeter.
Remote work blurred the company's security perimeter.
Attackers inside the perimeter can still cause harm.

cards.def:
Authorised simulated attacks to find weaknesses
हिंदी: अधिकृत नकली हमलों से कमज़ोरियाँ खोजना
examples: Penetration testing uncovered an exposed endpoint.
We hired an outside firm for penetration testing.
Penetration testing is required before the bank audit.
Fix all critical findings from penetration testing before launch.

cards.def:
A structured analysis of possible attacks
हिंदी: संभावित हमलों का विश्लेषण
examples: We built a threat model for the new service.
The threat model listed stolen passwords as the top risk.
Update the threat model when you add new features.
A threat model helps teams think like attackers.

cards.def:
Regularly replacing encryption keys
हिंदी: एन्क्रिप्शन कुंजियाँ नियमित बदलना
examples: Automatic key rotation reduced our risk.
Key rotation happens every ninety days.
Plan key rotation so it doesn't break running services.
The audit asked for evidence of key rotation.

cards.def:
Design that behaves as users expect
हिंदी: उपयोगकर्ता की अपेक्षा अनुसार व्यवहार
examples: An API should follow the principle of least astonishment.
A delete button that saves would break the principle of least astonishment.
Follow the principle of least astonishment when naming functions.
Good UX design respects the principle of least astonishment.

cards.def:
Using sensible defaults to reduce setup
हिंदी: सरल डिफ़ॉल्ट से सेटअप घटाना
examples: Spring Boot favours convention over configuration.
Rails is famous for convention over configuration.
Convention over configuration helps new joiners start quickly.
With convention over configuration, files go in standard folders.

cards.def:
Describing what is wanted rather than how to do it
हिंदी: क्या चाहिए बताने वाला (कैसे नहीं)
examples: Terraform uses a declarative style.
SQL is declarative; you say what data you want.
Kubernetes uses declarative files to describe the desired state.
Declarative code is often shorter and easier to read.

cards.def:
Describing step-by-step how to do something
हिंदी: कदम-दर-कदम निर्देश देने वाला
examples: The old script was imperative and hard to follow.
Imperative code lists each step in order.
Most beginners learn imperative programming first.
We replaced the imperative setup script with a config file.
